title: Elastic Stack (ELK) or Splunk: Log Analytics at Scale
excerpt: Both can collect, search and analyse huge volumes of logs. Elastic offers flexibility and lower cost at scale for teams that can run it; Splunk offers a polished, integrated product with strong enterprise support.
verdict: Elastic is far more economical for very large data volumes if you have a capable team to build and run it. Splunk is easier to get value from quickly and comes with comprehensive support, for organisations willing to pay more for an integrated product.

spec1.label: Cost at very large data volumes
spec1.device1Value: Much cheaper at very large scale
spec1.device2Value: Licence costs grow noticeably with volume or workload

spec2.label: Initial setup
spec2.device1Value: Several components to assemble (Elasticsearch, Logstash or Beats, Kibana)
spec2.device2Value: An integrated product, ready to use

spec3.label: Vendor support
spec3.device1Value: Available, but less comprehensive than fully commercial options
